picked.body: 기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 제조업이 15개월 연속 경기 확장 국면을 보이고 있는 가운데 지난 9월 구매관리자지수(PMI)가 소폭 하락하는 등 다소 주춤한 모습을 보였다. 미국 데이터 분석업체 S&P글로벌마켓인텔리전스(S&P Global Market Intelligence, 이하 S&P)가 1일 내놓은 ‘2026년 9월 베트남 제조업 PMI 보고서’에 따르면, 9월 PMI는 전월 대비 1.4포인트 내린 51.9를 나타냈으나, 일부 하락에도 불구하고 전반적인 경기 여건은 15개월 연속 개선세를 이어갔다. PMI는 각 기업 구매담당자 조사를 바탕으로 작성되는 업계 동향 지표로 50 미만은 경기 위축, 50 이상은 경기 확장을 의미한다. 지수는 △신규 주문 △생산 △고용 △공급업체 납품시간 △구매 재고 등의 5개 지표를 가중 평균한 값이다. 이번 지표는 △생산·신규 수주 증가세 둔화 △신규 수출주문 5개월 만에 최대 폭 감소 △유가·연료비 상승에 따른 투입가격 상승 속 판매단가 상승세 둔화 등 크게 3가지로 요약된다. 9월에도 제조업 생산은 뚜렷하게 늘어, 지난해 5월부터 시작된 증가세를 이어갔다. 다만 증가 속도는 8월보다 둔화했다. 조사에 참여한 기업들은 신규 수주 증가가 이번 생산 확대의 배경이라고 답했지만, 증가 속도는 둔화되는 모습을 보였다. 실제로 이번 신규 수주 증가폭은 5개월째 이어진 증가세 가운데 가장 약한 수준이었다. 신규 주문 수주가 늘었다고 답한 기업들은 시장 여건 개선과 거래처의 주문 규모 확대를 이유로 들었다. 수요 부진이 다시금 확인되면서 신규 수출 주문은 두 달 연속 감소세를 보였다. 해외발 신규 수주는 뚜렷하게 줄었는데, 속도는 지난 4월 이후 가장 빨랐다. 미처리 업무량은 앞선 두 달간 증가세를 보인 뒤 9월에는 전반적으로 큰 변화가 없었다. 일부 기업은 신규 수주 증가와 고용 감소가 겹치면서 생산 여력에 부담을 느꼈다고 답했지만, 다른 기업들은 신규 수주 증가세가 둔화한 덕분에 밀린 업무를 충분히 처리할 수 있었다고 밝혔다. 고용은 두 달 연속 감소세를 보였다.기업들은 직원 퇴사와 조직 개편이 겹친 결과라고 설명했다. 다만 9월 인력 감소 폭 자체는 미미한 수준에 그쳤다. 9월에도 구매활동은 뚜렷하게 늘었다. 기업들이 생산 확대를 뒷받침하기 위해 원자재 확보에 나선 결과다. 원자재가 계속 생산에 투입되면서 투입재 재고는 지속적으로 감소했다. 제조 업체들은 완제품 재고를 축소하려는 뚜렷한 움직임을 나타냈는데, 이를 위해 제품을 신속하게 출하했다. 실제로 완제품 재고는 지난 2011년 3월 조사가 시작된 이래 가장 빠른 속도로 줄었다. 한편 공급업체 납기는 다소 길어졌다. 기업들은 국제 운송 관련 문제와 악천후를 지연의 원인으로 지목했다. 투입비용이 추가로 오른 데에는 국제 정세가 핵심 요인으로 작용했다. 중동 전쟁이 연료·유가를 끌어올렸고, 이로 인해 운송비가 상승했다. 투입가격 상승 속도는 뚜렷했고 8월보다 다소 가팔랐지만, 최근 1년간 상승 폭 중에서는 여전히 가장 낮은 수준을 유지했다. 반면 판매단가 상승 속도는 5개월 연속 둔화하며 지난해 6월 이후 가장 약한 수준을 기록했다. 치열한 경쟁이 기업들의 비용 전가 능력을 제한한 영향이다. 시장 여건이 개선될 것이라는 기대는 향후 1년간 생산이 늘어날 것이라는 전망에 힘을 보탰다. 신제품 출시 계획 역시 낙관적인 전망의 배경이 되면서, 기업심리는 지난 2월 이후 가장 높은 수준으로 올라섰다. 이번 조사 결과에 대해 앤드류 하커(Andrew Harker) S&P 경제 이사는 “이러한 어려움에도 불구하고 생산은 뚜렷한 증가세를 보였고, 기업들은 향후 1년 전망에 대해 더 낙관적인 태도를 보였다"며 “PMI와 공식 통계 간의 과거 상관관계를 고려할 때, 제조업은 3분기 경제 성장에 견조하게 기여할 것으로 예상되며, 국제 정세가 개선될 경우 성장세가 한층 강화될 가능성도 충분하다”고 분석했다.

picked.t: Flooding, gridlock stretch from downtown HCMC through expat area
picked.body: A heavy downpour that began shortly after 5 p.m. and lasted nearly two hours caused severe traffic congestion in downtown Ho Chi Minh City. By 7 p.m., a traffic jam stretching more than 4 kilometers had formed from the Hang Xanh area to Saigon Bridge, a major route linking the city center with Thu Duc via Vo Nguyen Giap Street and Hanoi Highway. Nearby Nguyen Huu Canh Street was also heavily congested. A long line of traffic was moving slowly along Vo Nguyen Giap Street, near Saigon Bridge. The lane reserved for motorbikes began to flood after nearly an hour of heavy rain. A long line of traffic was moving slowly along Vo Nguyen Giap Street, near Saigon Bridge. The lane reserved for motorbikes began to flood after nearly an hour of heavy rain. A long line of traffic was moving slowly along Vo Nguyen Giap Street, near Saigon Bridge. The lane reserved for motorbikes began to flood after nearly an hour of heavy rain. Flooding on Nguyen Huu Canh Street, not far from Vietnam's tallest skyscraper Landmark 81, made traffic movement difficult. The densely populated area, which is home to numerous high-rise buildings, frequently experiences congestion during heavy rain at rush hour. Nearly 2 kilometers from Nguyen Huu Canh, Quoc Huong Street in the former District 2 saw floodwaters rise to nearly a meter during the rain, causing numerous vehicles to stall. Residents had to call for roadside assistance or push their vehicles through the flooded street. Situated near the Saigon River, the area is home to HCMC's largest expat community and is one of the city's major flood hotspots. At 6 p.m., more than 10 kilometers from Nguyen Huu Canh, cars and motorbikes were gridlocked across all six lanes of Pham Van Dong Street along a roughly 2-kilometer stretch between the Le Quang Dinh intersection and the Nguyen Thai Son six-way intersection. Traffic congestion typically begins early in this area.Pham Van Dong is a major artery connecting Thu Duc with Tan Son Nhat Airport. A line of vehicles with headlights on stretched along the road leading to Tan Son Nhat Airport. Tan Son Nhat, Vietnam's busiest airport, handled around 42.5 million passengers in 2025, roughly 10 million more than Hanoi's Noi Bai. Heavy rain already hit large parts of HCMC on Wednesday evening rush hour, leaving many streets deeply flooded, stalling vehicles and causing prolonged congestion. The city's Traffic and Technical Infrastructure Management Center said heavy rain combined with high tides overwhelmed drainage systems in several areas. At least 12 streets under the center's management were badly flooded. A section of Phan Huy Ich Street was submerged more than 1 m deep, with water pouring into buses and homes. An ambulance is trapped among motorbikes, its siren wailing nonstop with no room left to get through.

picked.t: Japanese retail giant Aeon targets 300 supermarkets, 30 shopping malls in Vietnam
picked.body: Under its medium-term business plan through March 2031, Aeon aims to generate more than 300 billion yen (US$1.9 billion) in operating revenue in Vietnam, 2.5 times higher than its fiscal year 2026 forecast. The group plans to increase its supermarket network, including MaxValu, from about 60 stores to 300, while allocating about 60% of its Southeast Asian investment to Vietnam. The group plans to expand its shopping mall network to 30 by the end of fiscal year 2030, while developing new facilities in Ha Long, Thanh Hoa and Da Nang. As of February 2026, Aeon operated 302 stores in Vietnam, including shopping malls, supermarkets and Ministop convenience stores. Aeon also sees MaxValu as a key growth driver, as its smaller stores can be opened more quickly in densely populated residential areas, particularly as large apartment complexes expand into suburban areas. Vietnam is also becoming an important production base for Aeon's private-label products. The group aims to raise the share of such products in its portfolio to 20%, from 6% currently, and increase sourcing from Vietnam for markets including Japan. Daisuke Tezuka, the executive officer in charge of Aeon's Vietnam business, told Nikkei Asia in early September that Vietnam's growing population, young consumers, and rising purchasing power offered substantial growth opportunities. According to the World Bank, Vietnam's GDP per capita reached US$5,066 in 2025, seven times higher than two decades earlier. Aeon entered Vietnam in 2014 and has since viewed the Southeast Asian country as a strategic market. Tezuka said the group's success over the past decade had strengthened its confidence in further expanding its business there. The group is also building a customer ecosystem through its Waon loyalty program, which has attracted around 4 million members since its wider rollout in Vietnam in 2025. With financial services planned for 2027, Aeon aims to increase membership to 20 million by fiscal year 2030. Other retailers are also expanding in Vietnam. Thailand's Central Retail plans to open up to 12 large supermarkets and double its store network over the next three years, while Masan Group aims to operate 10,000 WinMart+ stores by 2030. Japanese retailers, including Takashimaya and FamilyMart, are likewise seeking further growth opportunities in the Vietnamese market.

picked.t: One reason many SMEs struggle to scale, according to business advisors
picked.body: In the early stages, SME founders are often among their companies' greatest strengths. They know customers, make quick decisions and solve problems themselves. But as a business expands, this hands-on model can become difficult to sustain. When the founder becomes a bottleneck Yeo Kee Heng, known as Francis, is an MBA student at British University Vietnam (BUV) who runs a technology consulting business in Singapore with an established client base. For years, he viewed smooth daily operations as a sign of effective management. As the business grew, however, operational issues consumed more of his time, leaving less room for strategic planning. "I realized I had become good at managing the day-to-day operation, but that was different from truly leading a business. I needed to think strategically and learn how to lead change," Francis said. His experience reflects a broader challenge for founder-led businesses. When decision-making remains concentrated at the top, employees can become accustomed to waiting for approval rather than taking ownership, while the founder becomes increasingly tied to day-to-day operations. This challenge was described as an "execution gap" at SME Forum 2026, where business leaders and experts discussed the importance of organizational structures and operating systems as companies expand. Dao Gia Hung, Head of VPBank SME, said some Vietnamese businesses have grown from small companies into enterprises worth hundreds or thousands of billions of dong, while others have stalled despite similar market opportunities. "The difference is not market opportunity, but the ability to execute and adapt," he said. "Without agility and continuous innovation, businesses can easily fall behind as competition intensifies." Scaling, therefore, requires more than increasing sales or hiring employees. Founders eventually need to shift from solving problems themselves to building teams and systems that can do so independently. Growing as a leader For some business owners, management education can help with that transition. But returning to university while running a company can be difficult, making flexible and applied programs particularly relevant. British University Vietnam offers the MSc International Business Management (MIBM), targeting working professionals and business owners. The program is delivered in Vietnam over 12 months, shorter than many international master's programs that typically take around two years. Under the dual-degree program, graduates will receive master's degrees from both BUV and Manchester Metropolitan University. BUV was included in the QS Global MBA Rankings for the second consecutive year in September 2026, ranking 41st in Asia. Manchester Metropolitan University, meanwhile, has a Triple Crown-accredited business school, holding the three major international business school accreditations. The MIBM covers international business strategy, finance, operations, project management, data analytics and emerging markets. Case studies, simulations and applied projects expose students to strategic decisions relevant to business owners. International study tours offer exposure to different business environments, including developments in technology and artificial intelligence. Through BUV's network of more than 500 corporate partners, students can also meet industry experts and senior executives. "At BUV, learning does not come only from textbooks," Francis said. "We have opportunities to meet experts and senior business leaders whom we would otherwise rarely have access to and to learn directly from their experience." For SME owners, sustainable growth depends not only on how much work a founder can handle but also on whether the business can operate without constant reliance on one person. The transition requires founders to move from personally keeping the business running to building the teams, systems and strategic direction needed for further growth. Learn more about the MSc International Business Management (MIBM) here .

picked.t: F&B market grows amid intensifying competition
picked.body: The number of food service outlets rose to about 329,200 by the end of the second quarter from around 299,900 a year earlier, adding nearly 30,000 outlets to the market, according to a recent report by iPOS.vn and Nestlé Professional. That means a larger share of total industry revenue is being spread across a significantly greater number of businesses, leaving many individual operators with little improvement in sales despite growth in the overall market. The divergence underscores the pressure facing Vietnam’s F&B sector after a year of intense consolidation, as new outlets increasingly compete for the same pool of consumers. Nguyen Do Anh Quan, brand director at iPOS.vn, said the first half of the year is typically a period of market consolidation. "After the Lunar New Year holiday, outlets with weak cash flows or an unstable operating foundation often have to leave the market," Quan said. The total number of outlets declined just 0.1% from the end of 2025, suggesting closures have slowed while new openings have been sufficient to offset most businesses leaving the market, he said. "This can also be seen as a sign that the market is gradually becoming more stable, while F&B businesses are beginning to operate in a more structured, professional and planned manner," Quan said. The revenue growth also needs to be viewed against seasonal and price factors. The 2025 Lunar New Year's timing split the peak shopping season between December 2024 and January 2025 while most of the peak consumption period for 2026's Lunar New Year fell within the first half. Consumer prices rose 4.4% year-on-year on average in the first half of 2026. This suggests that part of the increase in F&B revenue reflected higher prices and broader macroeconomic factors, rather than a corresponding increase in real consumer demand. The strain on individual businesses is reflected in a survey of 481 F&B operators across 15 provinces and cities. About 43% reported lower revenue than a year earlier. Of these, 27.5% recorded declines of 5-20% but remained in operation, while 15.2% suffered declines of more than 20% and faced significant difficulties. At the other end of the spectrum, 20.2% of businesses reported revenue growth of more than 5%, while 37.1% saw relatively stable revenue. The figures suggest that consumer spending has not disappeared from the market, but is being allocated more selectively. Even businesses operating in the same area and facing similar cost structures and customer demographics can post sharply different results. Vu Thanh Hung, CEO of iPOS.vn, was quoted by Dau tu (Investment) newspaper as saying that consumers were still eating and drinking outside the home and were even spending more, but were becoming more selective and demanding . "Total spending has not left the market, it has simply changed destinations," Hung said. He said the reallocation of consumer spending helps explain why businesses operating under similar conditions have achieved markedly different results over the past six months. The divergence is particularly visible between F&B businesses. While the share of outlets reporting declining revenue was broadly similar in the two segments, food businesses recorded stronger growth. Some 25.6% of food businesses reported growth of more than 5%, compared with 15.8% among beverage outlets. Food businesses can rely on demand for meals, group dining and bundled products to increase average bill values. Beverage outlets, by contrast, face intense competition for each upsizing decision, additional topping or attempt to persuade customers to choose a higher-priced drink. Pressure is also coming from a growing number of mass-market and low-cost models . Some 88.5% of surveyed owners said they had clearly seen such models emerge around their business areas, while about 58.2% said they had actually felt the pressure. Some 35.4% of outlets kept their existing sales approach and accepted losing some customers, while 22.8% proactively cut prices, introduced promotions or added lower-priced products. The trend suggests low-cost models have not yet forced the entire market into across-the-board price cuts, but are gradually taking customers away from outlets that are slow to adapt.

picked.t: Ho Chi Minh City faces severe rain and flooding risks through Oct 6
picked.body: According to the Southern Regional Hydro-Meteorological Station, the city will experience strong daytime sunshine followed by late-afternoon and evening showers from Oct. 1 to Oct. 4. Residents are advised to prepare for extreme downpours accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning caused by thermal convection. The rain will be largely concentrated in the former districts of Go Vap, Cu Chi, Hoc Mon, and District 12, though central areas could also see localized heavy rain by Oct. 2. Tran Van Hung, deputy director of the station, warned that a low-pressure trough is expected to strengthen into an intertropical convergence zone and increase rainfall on Oct. 5 and 6. He noted that the city is currently at the peak of its rainy season. While October will see frequent downpours, the total monthly rainfall is forecast to remain around the long-term average with no signs of unusual conditions. The incoming storms follow a massive deluge on the afternoon and evening of Sept. 30 that brought 136 mm of rain to Le Minh Xuan station, 108 mm to Thu Duc, 101 mm to Ben Cat, and 100 mm to An Phu. The downpour coincided with high tides, overwhelming local drainage systems and severely flooding at least 12 roads, causing severe traffic jams as it happened during evening rush hour. On Phan Huy Ich Street, floodwaters surpassed one meter in some sections, inundating buses and residential properties. Authorities determined that the severe flooding on this road was exacerbated by dredged materials from the Tham Luong–Ben Cat–Nuoc Len Canal project. The materials being stored temporarily in the canal narrowed the waterway and caused water to flow back into drainage pipes, which severely reduced their capacity. As of noon on Oct. 1, some residential areas in Thu Duc remained heavily flooded. Relevant agencies are operating pumping stations and tide-control gates while inspecting construction sites that may be obstructing drainage. The city currently monitors 159 locations prone to recurring flooding, including 76 in the former Ho Chi Minh City, 52 in the former Binh Duong Province, and 31 in the former Ba Ria-Vung Tau Province. The latter two were merged into HCMC last year.

picked.t: Singapore homegrown restaurant brand Crystal Jade's holding firms placed under receivership
picked.body: Kroll said in a news release on Wednesday that its representatives had been appointed receivers of Crystal Jade Culinary Concepts Holding Pte Ltd and Crystal Jade Culinary Concepts Holding (Great China) Limited, which are the holding firms for the group’s restaurant operations in Singapore and Hong Kong respectively, Channel News Asia reported. A receivership typically gives an independent party control over some or all of a company’s assets, often when the company is unable to meet its financial obligations. Kroll’s representatives are examining Crystal Jade’s financial and operational affairs and evaluating strategic options for its portfolio of brands, restaurants and businesses to stabilize the group and preserve its value, the advisory firm said, adding that it would engage stakeholders on potential restructuring as and when appropriate. Kroll representatives confirmed that Crystal Jade is not exiting the food and beverage market, and the restaurant group also said its restaurants remain open, according to The Straits Times . Established in Singapore in 1991, Crystal Jade expanded over the years with multiple dining concepts both in Singapore and overseas markets, including China, South Korea and Vietnam. Its Singapore operations comprise six restaurant brands, ranging from Cantonese fine dining to casual noodle, dim sum and other Chinese cuisine concepts. Its Crystal Jade Golden Palace restaurant at The Paragon mall was awarded one Michelin star from 2016 to 2018. The group has closed five outlets in Singapore this year as part of an ongoing review of its operations and outlet network, leaving 13 outlets in the city-state. A subsidiary, Crystal Jade Fine Dining, was earlier this year charged over failing to file its complete income tax return on time without a reasonable excuse, which could result in a fine of up to S$5,000 (US$3,900) if found guilty.

picked.t: What has driven Vietnam to its highest tourism development ranking since 2019?
picked.body: Emis, a French tourist who recently visited Ho Chi Minh City, said she was impressed by Vietnam's safety and the friendliness of its people amid global instability. "Vietnam is very safe. I feel safe walking on the streets and comfortable talking to locals," she said. She also praised the country's relaxed visa policies and modern infrastructure in HCMC. Vietnam climbed seven places to 52nd among 110 economies in the World Economic Forum's 2026 Travel and Tourism Development Index, its highest ranking since the Covid-19 pandemic. Industry insiders attributed the improvement to several factors, including visa reforms, infrastructure upgrades, expanding tourism offerings and reputation for safety. "Vietnam's improvement is the result of several developments coming together rather than one single factor. Visa reform has certainly been one of the most important," Martin Koerner, commercial director of The Anam Group, a chain of luxury resort hotels in Vietnam, told VnExpress International . Vietnam has made it easier for international visitors to enter and stay in the country, including through 90-day e-visas and 45-day visa exemptions for citizens of 24 countries, including major economies like France, the U.K., the Netherlands and Russia. Koerner said Vietnam has also invested heavily in aviation and transport infrastructure. Upgraded airport terminals and improved domestic connectivity have helped address one of the country's longstanding tourism constraints, he said. Major projects are expected to further improve accessibility. Long Thanh International Airport in Dong Nai City, next to Ho Chi Minh City, is slated to begin commercial operations in December and replace Tan Son Nhat as Vietnam's largest aviation hub. Diverse tourism offerings Infrastructure and easier access have been accompanied by an expansion of tourism products, particularly in food, wellness, adventure and nature-based tourism. Dr. Justin Matthew Pang, senior program manager of the Tourism and Hospitality Management program at RMIT Vietnam, said Vietnam had made significant progress in both its tourism offerings and policy development. Vietnamese cuisine has gained greater international recognition, with more local restaurants receiving international accolades, including Michelin Guide recognition, he said. "There have been more tourism offerings ranging from attractions to resorts from Nha Trang, Mu Cang Chai, Moc Chau, Phong Nha - Ke Bang. These offerings have put Vietnam on the map, and these emerging destinations offer more wellness, adventure, beach and rustic activities," Pang said. Vietnam performed strongly in areas including price competitiveness, air transport, port infrastructure, natural resources, and safety and security in this year's WEF index. Koerner said geopolitical developments had affected travel patterns. Global uncertainty, including the conflict in the Middle East, has disrupted traditional travel routes and shifted some demand toward destinations in Southeast Asia. Vietnam is well positioned in this environment because it is perceived as "a safe, stable and good-value destination," he said. Despite the improvement, Vietnam still ranked behind several Southeast Asian tourism markets. Singapore placed 13th globally, followed by Indonesia at 23rd, Malaysia at 26th and Thailand at 38th. Industry insiders said Vietnam needs further improvements to strengthen its position and compete more effectively with regional tourism destinations. "The result reflects both broader changes in the global tourism environment and some improvements within Vietnam. The more important question is whether Vietnam can turn this momentum into sustainable tourism competitiveness," said Dr. Matt Kim, a lecturer in the Tourism and Hospitality Management program at RMIT Vietnam. Koerner said Vietnam could move further up the rankings by combining infrastructure investment and easier access with environmental sustainability, consistent service standards and stronger international marketing.

picked.t: 베트남, ‘유류세’ 0% 한시적 면세 조치 연장…9→12월 말까지
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시의 한 주유소에서 주유 중인 그랩기사. 베트남이 유류세 한시적 면세 조치의 3개월 연장을 결정했다. 이에 따라 현재 시행 중인 휘발유와 경유에 대한 환경세와 부가세 면제 조치는 연말까지 이어진다. 베트남 정부는 지난달 30일 결의안 제43/2026/NQ-CP호를 통해 연료 제품에 부과되는 △수입 관세 △환경보호세(환경세) △부가세 감면 조치를 연말까지 3개월간 연장을 결정했다. 이번 결의안은 지난 3월 9일자 시행령 제72/2026/ND-CP호와 4월 30일자 결의안 제25/2026/NQ-CP호에서 규정한 조치를 연장한다는 내용을 담고 있다. 이 중 시행령 제72호는 석유제품에 대한 수입 관세의 0% 인하를 골자로 한다. 이에 따라 휘발유와 석유화학 원료인 나프타·리포메이트 등에 대한 관세는 기존 10%에서 0%로 인하됐고, 경유·연료유·항공유·등유 등에 대한 수입 관세 역시 7%에서 0%로 인하됐다. 자일렌·컨덴세이트·파라자일렌 등 일부 석유화학 원료의 수입 관세는 3%에서 0%로, 순환 탄화수소는 2%에서 0%로 각각 인하됐다. 이 조치들은 당초 3월 9일부터 4월 30일까지 시행될 예정이었으나, 이후 6월 30일, 9월 30일 등으로 지속 연장됐다. 앞서 정부는 지난 2월 말 미국·이스라엘과 이란 간 중동 분쟁으로 인해 석유제품 가격이 급등하자 시장 충격을 최소화하기 위해 지난 3월부터 유류세 한시적 면제 조치 시행에 나선 뒤 정책 연장을 지속하고 있다. 또한 이번 결의안 제43호는 국회 결의안 제19/2026/QH16호에서 규정한 휘발유·경유·등유·연료유·항공유에 대한 환경세·부가세 면제 기한을 오는 12월 31일까지 연장한다는 내용이 담겼다. 해당 결의안은 휘발유(에탄올 제외)와 경유·등유·연료유·항공유 대한 환경세를 L당 0%로, 부가세 또한 별도 신고 및 납부 없이 매입세액 공제가 가능하도록 규정하고 있다. 이에 대해 베트남 재무부는 “국제유가 변동성과 중동 정세 불안이 이어지는 상황에서 이번 세제 조치 연장이 에너지 안보를 지키고 거시경제 안정과 물가 관리를 뒷받침하며, 생산·경영 활동 회복에도 도움이 될 것”이라고 설명했다. 재무부는 이어 “이번 조치가 연료 기업들의 수입처 다변화를 유도해 기존 공급시장 의존도를 낮추고, 국내 연료 공급을 안정적으로 유지하는 데도 도움이 될 것”이라고 덧붙였다. 공상부는 경제 발전과 에너지 안보, 국내 연료 시장 안정을 위해 필요하다고 판단될 경우 이번 조치의 적용 기간을 단축하거나 추가로 연장하는 방안을 제안할 수 있다.

기사 이해를 돕기위해 AI를 활용해 제작한 이미지입니다. 베트남 하노이증시(HNX)에서 거래 중인 전 종목이 오는 12월 말 호치민증시(HoSE)로 모두 이전상장될 예정이다. 이는 증권 당국의 시장 구조조정 계획에 따라 하노이증시를 채권이나 파생상품, 비상장주식 거래 시장으로 운영하기 위한 것으로, 투자자들이 보유한 주식에는 영향을 주지 않는다. 베트남증권거래소(VNX)는 최근 시장 구조조정 로드맵에 따라 하노이증시 상장 종목의 호치민증시 이전상장 세부 일정을 발표했다. 이에 따라 중소형주 중심의 하노이증시의 모든 상장 종목은 오는 12월 28일부터 호치민증시로 이전상장돼 거래될 예정이다. 현재 하노이증시에 상장 중인 종목은 299개로, 섹터별로는 공업이 91개로 가장 많고, 건설업 42개, 상업·서비스업이 34개로 뒤를 잇고 있다. 구체적으로, 하노이증시에서의 마지막 거래일은 12월 23일로, 24~25일 양일간 거래가 중단된 뒤, 28일부터 호치민증시에서 이전상장된 종목들의 매매가 재개된다. 이에 대해 베트남증권거래소는 “이번 이전상장은 거래 시장만 바뀌는 것으로 투자자가 보유한 주식 자체에는 직접적인 영향이 없다”고 밝혔다. 당국에 따르면, 이번 하노이증시의 이전상장은 두 거래소의 기능과 역할을 명확히 나누기 위한 조치다. 앞으로 호치민증시는 △주식 △펀드 △주식워런트증권 거래를 전담하고 하노이증시는 △채권 △파생상품 △비상장주식 △탄소배출권 거래를 담당할 예정이다. 한편, 현재 시장별 가격제한폭은 호치민증시가 일 ±7%, 하노이증시는 ±10%이다. 베트남증권거래소는 이전상장 이후 가격제한폭 조정에 관한 내용은 발표하지 않았다. 베트남증권거래소는 100% 국영기업으로, 호치민증시와 하노이증시를 운영하고 있다.
